A player passes in to the middle player, who sets it straight back. The attacker now has two options and about a second to choose: **chip** it over them into the empty goal, or **take it round** and roll it in.

After the attempt, the middle player joins a line and the attacker becomes the new keeper. It keeps rotating and everybody does both jobs.
drills.setup: An area with a goal at each end and one player in the middle. Two lines of players with a ball each.
coachingPoints: Decide as the set-back is travelling, not when it arrives
Chip: get under it with a firm, stabbing contact — do not scoop
Round them: take the first touch wide of their reach, not straight at them
If they come out fast, the chip is on; if they stay, go round
progressions: Keeper backs away facing the ball, forcing the chip
Keeper rushes out, forcing the 1v1
Middle player defends properly and a real keeper goes in goal
regressions: Move the goals closer together
Keeper stays on their line

diagram.caption: Set back, then chip or take them round.

drills.name: Finishing Bingo
drills.summary: A game where the team must score with every type of finish on the list.
drills.description:
Write a list somewhere both teams can see it: header, volley, half-volley, first time, outside of the foot, laces, weak foot, one from outside the box.

Play a normal game. Each team ticks off a finish type when they score with it, and the first team to complete the whole list wins. Repeating one you already have counts for nothing.

It gets players trying finishes they would otherwise avoid — especially the weak-foot one, which is usually the last box anyone fills.
drills.setup: A small pitch, goal at each end, keepers. Bibs. A whiteboard or a piece of paper on a cone with the list on it.
coachingPoints: Look at the list before you shoot — which one do you still need?
Set each other up: someone has to cross for the header
Weak foot early, while the game is still open
Do not force a volley from a bad position just to tick it off
progressions: Individuals complete their own list rather than the team
Three in a row on the list wins it
regressions: Shorter list
Any goal counts once the team has three types

diagram.caption: Tick off every finish type on the list.

drills.name: Out and Back
drills.summary: Dribble inside a box until the call, then out around a far cone and back in.
drills.description:
Mark a small square inside a much bigger one, with tall cones on the outer square. Everyone dribbles inside the small square.

On the call, they take the ball out, round any one of the outer cones, and back into the middle. First one back wins that round.

It is a simple warm-up but it does two things at once: close control in a crowd, then a proper long carry at speed. Players who take tiny touches on the way out lose every time, which teaches the difference faster than saying it.
drills.setup: A 10x10 square inside a 25x25 one, with a large cone at each corner and midpoint of the outer square. One ball per player.
coachingPoints: Small touches inside, big ones the moment you are out
Pick your cone before the whistle so you are not deciding at the exit
Head up — everyone is leaving at once
Turn tight around the cone, do not run a wide arc
progressions: Round two cones before coming back
Call a specific cone as they set off
regressions: Leave the ball in the box, run round a cone and come back to it
Fewer players in the middle square

diagram.caption: Out around a cone, then straight back in.

drills.name: Run the Lines
drills.summary: Beat two defenders who can only move along their own line, then finish.
drills.description:
A grid split into thirds by two lines across it, with a goal at the far end. A defender stands on each line and cannot leave it; a third defends the goal.

The attacker has to beat both line defenders, then the last one, to score. Because the line players can only slide sideways, the attacker beats them with timing and a change of direction rather than pace alone.

If a defender wins it, they pass it up to the next defender, who dribbles out over the end line — so there is something in it for them too.
drills.setup: A 20x20 grid with two lines marked across it and a goal at one end. One defender on each line, one in front of the goal. Attackers queue at the far end with a ball each.
coachingPoints: Attack the line at an angle, not straight on
Change direction late — the first move should be a lie
Once you are through one line, go; the next defender is already moving
Line defenders: shuffle, do not cross your feet
progressions: Two or three attackers go at once
Make it multi-directional — travel side to side repeatedly
Defenders may defend a whole third rather than a line
regressions: Only one line defender
Defenders press but cannot tackle

diagram.caption: Two line defenders, then the last one.

drills.name: Share or Beat
drills.summary: Two attackers against one defender: pass around them, or take them on.
drills.description:
A goal and keeper at each end with one defender in front of each. Attackers work in pairs from the halfway line.

The keeper rolls it out to one of the pair, and it becomes a 2v1 towards the far goal. Every time, there is the same question: **share it** with your partner and go round the defender, or **beat them yourself**.

Both answers are right depending on what the defender does, which is the whole lesson. A defender who commits to the ball should be passed around; one who sits off and covers the pass should be taken on.
drills.setup: A pitch with a goal and keeper at each end, one defender in front of each goal. Two groups of attackers at the halfway line, split into pairs.
coachingPoints: Look at the defender, not your partner — they tell you which option is on
If they come to you, the pass is on; if they sit off, go at them
Supporting player: stay wide enough to be a real option, not right beside them
Take the shot early once you are past — the cover arrives fast
progressions: Make it 2v2
Add a time limit on each attack
regressions: Play it as a 3v1
Defender may not tackle, only press

diagram.caption: Pass around them, or take them on.

drills.name: One Per Box
drills.summary: Three teams in four boxes, and you can never be in the same box as a team-mate.
drills.description:
Split a square into four boxes. Three teams of three, a ball between each team. Players pass or carry the ball from box to box — but **no two team-mates may ever be in the same box**.

That single rule keeps everyone moving. The moment you receive, someone else on your team has to leave, and you have to look up to see where the space actually is.

Start it unopposed with all three teams working at once, then make one team the defenders and play two against one.
drills.setup: A 20x20 square split into four boxes. Three teams of three, one ball each to start. Bibs in three colours.
coachingPoints: Check the box before you move into it — is one of yours already there?
Receive on the half-turn so you can see the next box
Move as soon as you have passed, do not admire it
Talk: tell them which box you are heading for
progressions: One team defends and it becomes two against one
Lose the ball and your team becomes the defenders
Being caught in a box with a team-mate concedes possession
regressions: Throw and catch rather than pass
Bigger boxes

diagram.caption: Never two team-mates in the same box.

drills.name: Score From the Box
drills.summary: Four goals, six zones, and you can only score from the box in front of a goal.
drills.description:
A rectangle split into six boxes — three across, two deep — with a goal on each side at both ends. Four a side.

You can only score from inside the box directly in front of the goal you are attacking. With two goals at each end and three channels to work in, the attacking team is looking to get an extra player into one channel; the defending team is trying to cover two of the three and stay compact.

That trade-off — spread out to attack, squeeze to defend — is the whole game, and it shows up in almost every phase of real football.
drills.setup: A 40 x 20 area split into six boxes. Two goals on each end line, wide apart. Four a side, bibs.
coachingPoints: Attacking: get width in all three channels and find the spare player
Defending: pick two channels and stay connected — you cannot cover all three
Switch it when one side gets crowded; the far goal will be free
You have to be in the box to score, so time the run rather than camping there
progressions: Score more points for a bigger overload in the channel
Winner stays on
You must find a target player before you can score
regressions: Score from anywhere on the pitch
Add two more goals in the middle channel
Play it unopposed to learn the shape

diagram.caption: Only the box in front of the goal counts.
